$comment: RF Prescription / Severity / Recovery Rule Pack v1. EVIDENCE-EXTRACTED, NON-EXECUTABLE. Source-of-truth rules for the FUTURE functional Rectus Femoris beta engine. Numbers (dosage, recovery dates, thresholds) are PROHIBITED as universal evidence by RF v1.2 (RF-REHAB-004 / §9.8 / §12.3) and are therefore authored as STRUCTURE with explicit gap markers. Structure (six-phase Aspetar model, severity classification ontology, field milestones, adaptation actions) is evidence-supported. Not wired to runtime. Does not import legacy code. Does not mutate any RF knowledge object.

governance.created_for: Bridge layer between the governed RF knowledge system and the future RF beta plan/session engine. Defines severity, confidence, recovery-window, phase, dosage, progression, regression, daily-check-in, and exercise/activity mapping rules with evidence provenance. NOT an engine; NOT runtime.
governance.non_inheritance_statement: Numeric values in legacy data/injuryKnowledge/quadriceps.js and lib/injuryEngine/* are NOT treated as evidence-backed RF rules. Where a legacy number is shown it is labelled legacy_reference_not_evidence_backed and the rule's evidence_status remains gap or extrapolated.
governance.boundary_statement: This rule pack is data only. It imports no module. It mutates no RF-EX / RF-ACT / RF-ASSESS / CAP / evidence-linking / RF-rule / taxonomy object. It is quarantine-clean (no legacy dependency).

severity_rules.statement: Severity comes from assessment answers and evidence-backed severity/structural rules. Confidence is match quality. Confidence does NOT determine severity, and severity does NOT determine confidence.
severity_rules.self_report_constraint: Self-report alone must not assign current injury identity, structural severity, prognosis, progression speed, monitoring threshold, or readiness (RF v1.2 §9.6 No-independent-effect).

severity_rules.description: Qualitative functional-severity characterization from assessment observations (RF v1.2 §9.7). Bands are evidence-quality-tagged observation summaries, NOT an invented numeric score and NOT a structural grade.

bands.user_facing_wording: Milder pattern: movement and daily function are largely preserved.
assessment_answer_indicators: pain present but tolerable in daily tasks
pain_function_indicators: active knee-extension and hip-flexion largely preserved
bands.confidence_impact: no automatic confidence change (severity and confidence are independent)
bands.plan_impact: candidate Foundation/Reload entry, capacity-gated, never time-gated

bands.user_facing_wording: Moderate pattern: noticeable loss of movement, strength, or comfort.
strength_weakness_indicators: clear weakness resisting knee extension / hip flexion
bands.plan_impact: conservative Foundation entry, monitoring contract required

bands.user_facing_wording: Higher-concern pattern: please seek in-person review before progressing.
assessment_answer_indicators: unable to bear weight or straighten knee
mechanism_indicators: high-velocity injury with sudden loss of function
pain_function_indicators: unable to actively extend knee against gravity
strength_weakness_indicators: marked weakness suggesting higher-grade or tendon involvement
bands.confidence_impact: confidence is withheld/down-weighted in safety-sensitive states (policy §7a)
bands.plan_impact: REHAB_BLOCKED candidate; route to review; no autonomous plan

severity_rules.gap_notes: Band STRUCTURE is evidence-informed (§9.7 observation domains). Exact cut-offs that separate the bands are NOT established by the RF evidence set and remain a gap for clinician definition and validation.

severity_rules.description: A valid Munich classification may STRUCTURE the record and give population-limited group-level context only. Must not be inferred from mechanism/symptoms/self-test; medians must not become individual timelines.
severity_rules.plan_impact: record context only; widens uncertainty; does not alter stage or dosage autonomously
severity_rules.gap_notes: Classification ontology is direct; conversion to an individual RF recovery window/dosage is PROHIBITED and remains a gap.

severity_rules.description: Store a BAMIC grade/class only when supplied by a valid report. In a small elite cohort, valid MRI-confirmed grade may widen group-level return-to-full-training/repeat-injury uncertainty. No precise individual timeline or automatic severity conversion.
severity_rules.gap_notes: Ontology direct (E1); RF outcome context is bounded/population-limited; individual timeline is a gap.

severity_rules.description: Documented proximal central-aponeurosis involvement may increase prognostic caution vs distal involvement in a similar high-level population. Action: widen uncertainty, avoid early date promises. Do not automatically alter stage or dosage.

Pooled operative/nonoperative timelines are broad research benchmarks only. When management restrictions are unresolved, apply RF-SAF-006 and block generic rehabilitation. No treatment-superiority inference, individual prediction, or autonomous management choice.

Reported fibrosis/scar/lump/tightness is history provenance, NOT current severity. Store in injury_history_modifier with provenance and confirmation status. Self-report alone assigns no severity, prognosis, monitoring threshold, or readiness.

confidence_policy_references.principle: Confidence is match/evidence quality, not diagnostic certainty, capacity, readiness, progression, or clearance.

prohibited_values: never present as a clinical/diagnostic/readiness/clearance score

rf_factors_increasing_match_confidence: mechanism consistent with RF load (kicking, sprinting)
self-test pattern consistent across multiple RF-ASSESS items
confidence_policy_references.red_flag_withholding_behavior: If any RF-SAF red flag or high-concern severity is present, prefer a qualitative label and a visible review warning over any percentage (policy §7a; RF v1.2 §12.2). Confidence is withheld, not inflated.
confidence_policy_references.missing_data_cap: Materially incomplete assessment further lowers the cap and may force a qualitative-only result.
confidence_policy_references.conflicting_signal_cap: Conflicting signals force a lower cap and a review prompt.
confidence_policy_references.separation_statement: This rule pack does not re-implement the confidence policy; the engine must consume the policy doc as source of truth.

modifiers_that_lengthen: poor early walking/stairs tolerance and reduced active knee-extension function
modifiers_that_shorten: preserved early walking/stairs tolerance and active function (qualitative only)
good monitored load tolerance with appropriate next-day recovery
recovery_window_rules.user_facing_wording: Estimated recovery window for similar injury patterns. Actual recovery depends on severity, symptoms, sport demands, and clinician review.
prohibited_wording: You will return in X days/weeks
recovery_window_rules.research_benchmark_reference: Munich/Ekstrand and BAMIC cohort medians exist as GROUP context only (QRF-007/011/040/041/012/032). RF v1.2 §9.8 forbids presenting a precise individual return date from the current evidence set; medians must not become individual timelines.
recovery_window_rules.legacy_reference_not_evidence_backed: data/injuryKnowledge/quadriceps.js carries coarse week ranges; these are legacy, ungraded, and are NOT adopted as evidence-backed RF windows.
recovery_window_rules.gap_notes: No precise individual RF recovery window is authorized by current evidence. Only a qualitative, modifier-aware band with the mandated caveat wording may be shown, and only after the communication model is validated (RF v1.2 §9.8). Numeric min/max remain null pending governed, evidence-graded definition.

phase_model.phase_goal: Restore safe basic motion and early force tolerance.
entry_conditions: safety and restrictions resolved or being managed
phase_model.progression_criteria: Earlier safety and capability requirements satisfied with appropriate symptom response (criteria, not time).
phase_model.gap_notes: Six-phase Aspetar template is expert-informed structure (QRF-019 acceptability, not effectiveness). Exact capacity thresholds for exit are a gap.

exit_criteria: improving motion, force, execution, and response
phase_model.progression_criteria: Evidence across domains the next phase will load; not absence of pain alone.
phase_model.field_and_sport_exposure: mechanics drills and low-level locomotion when criteria permit

phase_model.phase_goal: Build strength, eccentric capacity, and running volume.
exit_criteria: repeated load tolerance and appropriate recovery
phase_model.progression_criteria: Includes Aspetar reference sprint-speed milestone ~70% of maximum at this phase exit (QRF-024), valid denominator only; not a universal mandatory threshold.
phase_model.regression_criteria: Inadequate recovery or symptom escalation with running volume.
phase_model.field_and_sport_exposure: generic running and low-intensity sport drills

phase_model.phase_goal: Prepare for higher-speed and higher-demand sport.
exit_criteria: clinical and field capacity sufficiently restored for higher exposures
withheld_exercise_families: full sprinting/kicking game scenarios (until Simulation criteria)
phase_model.progression_criteria: Aspetar reference sprint-speed milestone ~80% of maximum at this phase exit (QRF-024), valid denominator only.
phase_model.regression_criteria: Symptom or capacity regression with higher-speed exposure.
phase_model.field_and_sport_exposure: higher-speed running, acceleration/deceleration, higher-demand sport drills

phase_model.phase_goal: Reproduce sport scenarios, intensity, and volume.
exit_criteria: multi-domain Simulation evidence; demand profile substantially addressed
withheld_exercise_families: none specific; governed by safety/monitoring and concurrent-injury constraints
phase_model.progression_criteria: Aspetar reference ~95% of maximum sprint speed MAY contribute to Simulation evidence but cannot independently authorize unrestricted training/competition (RF-FIELD-002).
phase_model.regression_criteria: Failure under sport-specific demand or symptom escalation.
phase_model.field_and_sport_exposure: sprinting, kicking where relevant, game scenarios, worst-case demand blocks

phase_model.phase_goal: Return to performance and address residual deficits.
entry_conditions: readiness decision is a SEPARATE governed step, not granted here
exit_criteria: performance gaps, workload reintegration, and monitoring plan addressed
allowed_exercise_families: all families as appropriate under monitoring
capacity_targets: maintain or progress strength, power, speed, robustness
phase_model.regression_criteria: Residual deficit or workload-related symptom recurrence.
phase_model.field_and_sport_exposure: controlled or unrestricted team integration ONLY after a separate readiness decision (this rule pack does not grant it)
phase_model.gap_notes: Return-to-sport/readiness clearance is explicitly OUT of scope of this rule pack and of the engine it will power.

dosage_rules.statement: The RF module must NOT invent universal sets, repetitions, intensity, rest, weekly frequency, or progression increments. Any active universal RF dose without a separately approved, versioned source must fail content validation.

dosage_rules.intensity_qualitative: isometric-dominant, short-to-mid muscle length, low complexity, low effort
dosage_rules.session_placement: isolated motor control plus safe general strength
dosage_rules.stop_rule: governed by a configurable monitoring profile (acceptable during-session band + acceptable next-day change), NOT one global cut-off (RF v1.2 §12.3). Profile is not active until reviewed.
dosage_rules.alternative_rule: swap to an easier same-family RF-EX variant on poor tolerance (see exercise_family_mapping).
dosage_rules.legacy_reference_not_evidence_backed: legacy PHASE_RPE.protect = 'RPE 2-4' and legacy protect-phase sets/reps exist but are NOT adopted as evidence.
dosage_rules.gap_notes: Phase intensity CHARACTER is evidence-informed (isometric-dominant, short-mid length). Concrete sets/reps/hold/rest/frequency are NOT authorized by RF evidence and remain null gaps for clinician definition.

dosage_rules.intensity_qualitative: progressive range and load; tri-phasic exposure may be introduced; isolated plus controlled compound
dosage_rules.gap_notes: Loading character evidence-informed; numbers are gaps.

dosage_rules.intensity_qualitative: longer-length and eccentric-overload candidates with continued whole-limb strength; generic running volume
dosage_rules.session_placement: strength + eccentric + running volume composed into one weekly load plan (RF-REHAB-005)
dosage_rules.stop_rule: configurable monitoring profile; running and eccentric tracked as separate exposure domains (RF-RECUR-002)
dosage_rules.gap_notes: Eccentric overload character is evidence-informed; specific eccentric dose/sets/reps are gaps. Sprint milestone is a reference, not a mandatory threshold.

dosage_rules.intensity_qualitative: individualized strength, concentric and reactive qualities, continued eccentric capacity; higher-speed running
dosage_rules.stop_rule: configurable monitoring profile; high-speed exposure requires verified prerequisite capacity (RF-FIELD-003)

dosage_rules.intensity_qualitative: sport-specific power and reactive work; worst-case demand blocks; continuing strength
dosage_rules.session_placement: weekly load reconciliation; sprint/kick/COD as separate exposure domains
dosage_rules.stop_rule: configurable monitoring profile; 95% sprint speed is not sufficient alone (RF-FIELD-002)
dosage_rules.progression_trigger: multi-domain Simulation evidence + ~95% sprint-speed reference (QRF-025), contributory only
dosage_rules.high_caution_note: All high_caution_sport_specific_exposure RF-EX items remain manual_review_required and are NOT auto-prescribed; clinician sign-off required.

dosage_rules.intensity_qualitative: maintain or progress strength, power, speed, robustness
dosage_rules.progression_trigger: performance/monitoring based; NOT return-to-sport clearance (separate decision)

progression_rules.statement: Progression means movement WITHIN the rehab plan, not return-to-sport permission. Phase is determined by criteria and current capacity, not time alone. A later-phase entry requires evidence across the domains the next phase will load, not absence of pain alone. Safety/monitoring can override phase at any time.

review_gated_conditions: any active RF-SAF red flag blocks progression
progression_rules.gap_notes: Domains are evidence-informed; exact pass thresholds are a gap.

running_kicking_sprinting_restrictions: generic running only when criteria permit; no sprinting/kicking

required_assessment_evidence: repeated load tolerance with appropriate recovery
symptom_response_requirements: acceptable same-day response across running and eccentric domains
running_kicking_sprinting_restrictions: sprint-speed reference ~70% max (QRF-024), valid denominator only, NOT a mandatory universal threshold

required_assessment_evidence: clinical and field capacity restored for higher exposures
running_kicking_sprinting_restrictions: sprint-speed reference ~80% max (QRF-024); higher-speed exposure requires verified prerequisite capacity (RF-FIELD-003)
review_gated_conditions: safety override applies; high-caution items clinician-gated

required_assessment_evidence: multi-domain Simulation evidence; demand profile substantially addressed
running_kicking_sprinting_restrictions: ~95% sprint speed MAY contribute but is NOT sufficient alone (RF-FIELD-002)
review_gated_conditions: readiness/return-to-sport is a SEPARATE governed decision, not granted by progression

regression_rules.statement: Regression is a governed response, not failure. The engine may choose exactly ONE primary action after a session, traceable to specific inputs and rules.

regression_rules.same_day_response: mild increase within configurable acceptable band
regression_rules.action: maintain or reduce dose / reduce range or speed
regression_rules.what_to_simplify: today's targeted RF loading volume or range
regression_rules.what_to_withhold: the most demanding block of today's session
regression_rules.gap_notes: Action structure evidence-informed; the numeric band that defines 'mild' is a gap (configurable monitoring profile, not yet active).

regression_rules.pain_symptom_pattern: no red flags but clearly above band
regression_rules.action: replace with a regression / hold the current phase
regression_rules.what_to_simplify: swap to an easier same-family RF-EX alternative; reduce session demand

regression_rules.trigger: major deviation OR any red-flag / serious safety signal
regression_rules.same_day_response: major increase / sudden loss of function
regression_rules.pain_symptom_pattern: new progressive swelling, neuro/vascular symptoms, new pop with deterioration, inability to complete movement, any global red-flag match
regression_rules.action: regress phase / block rehabilitation and refer
regression_rules.what_to_withhold: withhold the session and show a review message

regression_rules.action: before referring, check the §12.5 non-response sequence (adherence, execution quality, actual-vs-prescribed load, symptom behavior/recovery window, diagnosis consistency, severity/stage consistency, new safety concerns, concurrent injuries, external load, population applicability)
regression_rules.non_response_threshold_note: The exact number of failed sessions or time window for non-response is an UNRESOLVED parameter and must not be invented (RF v1.2 §12.5).

daily_check_in_rules.statement: Daily check-in adjusts TODAY'S selected session only. It never rewrites future days, never changes phase by itself, and never grants progression or clearance.

daily_check_in_rules.check_in_response: green / within acceptable band, good recovery
daily_check_in_rules.allowed_adjustment: proceed with today's planned session as composed; minor within-session autoregulation only
daily_check_in_rules.not_allowed_adjustment: do not jump phases; do not unlock high-caution items; do not grant clearance

daily_check_in_rules.check_in_response: yellow / mild-to-moderate deviation or reduced confidence
daily_check_in_rules.allowed_adjustment: reduce today's volume / intensity / range or speed; swap to an easier same-family alternative; remove the most demanding block of today's session
daily_check_in_rules.not_allowed_adjustment: do not change future days; do not regress phase from a single yellow; do not add load
daily_check_in_rules.gap_notes: Band that triggers yellow is a configurable monitoring-profile gap.

daily_check_in_rules.check_in_response: red / major deviation or any safety/red-flag signal
daily_check_in_rules.allowed_adjustment: withhold today's session and show a review message; surface safety guidance
daily_check_in_rules.not_allowed_adjustment: do not auto-progress; do not reassure with a clearance/readiness statement; do not silently continue

exercise_family_mapping.reason: Mobility/movement-restoration items suit early safe motion (Foundation: restore basic motion).
Isometric-dominant / short-to-mid length core RF loading fits Foundation character.
Proximal hip/glute/trunk control supports the injured RF (athlete-system aware) without high RF tissue demand.
Controlled strength / running-prep foundations, criteria-gated, all manual_review_required (not auto-prescribed).
Running mechanics drills and low-level locomotion enter when Accumulation criteria permit.
Low-load conditioning supports volume without high RF tissue demand; available across phases where safe.

High-caution sport-specific exposures are listed for the Simulation phase but are WITHHELD by default and clinician-gated. They are never auto-prescribed by the engine; eligibility is empty until clinician sign-off (final_decision: high_caution_do_not_convert_yet).
Hold-for-review item; not mapped into an active phase until reviewed.

activity_exposure_mapping.name: Short-distance running exposure
activity_exposure_mapping.reason: Generic running enters in Accumulation when criteria permit.

activity_exposure_mapping.name: Acceleration exposure
activity_exposure_mapping.reason: Acceleration/deceleration belongs to higher-speed Transition exposures with verified prerequisite capacity.

activity_exposure_mapping.name: Static isolated kicking exposure
activity_exposure_mapping.reason: Kicking is a distinct exposure domain; tolerance of running does not clear kicking (RF-RECUR-002).

activity_exposure_mapping.name: Mixed generic and sport-specific running exposure
activity_exposure_mapping.reason: Blended running exposure as field capacity restores.

activity_exposure_mapping.name: High-speed running exposure
activity_exposure_mapping.reason: High-speed exposure requires verified prerequisite capacity; 95% sprint speed not sufficient alone.

activity_exposure_mapping.name: Elliptical conditioning
activity_exposure_mapping.reason: Low-impact conditioning supports volume without high RF tissue demand.

activity_exposure_statement: Activity exposure expresses capacity. It does not clear the athlete.

evidence_source_map.note: Every rule carries source_ids. QRF claim ids and grades are taken from the RF v1.2 evidence-claim annotations. Grade key: D = direct, C = comparative/cohort benchmark, I = indirect/limitation, E = expert/acceptability, X = excluded/very-weak. Where a canonical standalone QRF registry document is not yet linked in the repo, source mapping follow-up is flagged below. No evidence was invented.

QRF-019.context: six-phase Aspetar pathway practitioner acceptability (not effectiveness)

QRF-022.context: prohibition basis: no universal RF dosage

QRF-035.context: prohibition basis: no universal RF dosage

QRF-044.context: self-reported fibrosis is not severity (very weak)

source_mapping_followups: A canonical standalone QRF evidence-registry document is not separately linked in docs/; QRF grades here are extracted from the RF v1.2 inline evidence-claim annotations. Follow-up: link or author a single QRF registry file and cross-reference.
Munich/Ekstrand/BAMIC primary citations are listed in RF v1.2 §References (e.g. Ekstrand 2013, Reurink 2015) but are not yet machine-readable; follow-up: structured citation objects.
All dosage and recovery NUMBERS remain gaps; follow-up requires separately governed, evidence-graded, clinician-reviewed source before any number becomes active.
